name: Facet
text:
Implement a dark theme by default with a persistent light-theme toggle.

Dark themes reduce eye strain in low-light conditions and align with industry standards like Manus’ competitive analysis and Graphify’s dashboard. A persistent toggle lets users override the default without losing context. Trade-off: some users may prefer light themes universally, but the default balances accessibility with consistency.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users won’t switch from dark mode once set, making the toggle a dead switch, not a living control. Instead, default to system preference: if the OS is dark, use dark; if light, use light. That’s the standard, not a toggle. Settle it with A/B tests showing no measurable drop in user satisfaction or task completion between the two approaches.
